prompt: A farmer plants a vegetable garden near a forest where rabbits live. Rabbits eat many garden vegetables including lettuce, carrots, and beans. Which of the following plants would most likely survive in this garden?
optionA: A plant with bitter-tasting leaves and thorny stems
optionB: A leafy plant with tender, soft leaves and no protection
optionC: A climbing plant with smooth, juicy stems
optionD: A short plant with thin, delicate leaves
explanation: Plants with bitter taste or thorns protect themselves from being eaten by rabbits. Thorns and bad taste discourage animals from eating the plant.

prompt: A school installs panels on its roof to capture energy from the sun and turn it into electricity for the building. What type of energy resource does the sun provide?
optionA: Renewable
optionB: Nonrenewable
optionC: Fossil fuel
optionD: Limited to polar regions
explanation: The sun produces energy every day and will do so for billions of years. We can use this energy over and over, which makes it renewable.

prompt: A toy uses a hanging weight attached to a string to wind up and spin a propeller, until the weight reaches the ground. Which change would make the propeller spin for a longer time before stopping?
optionA: Using a thicker, heavier string
optionB: Making the propeller blades smaller
optionC: Releasing the weight from a greater height
optionD: Replacing the weight with a lighter one
explanation: When the weight falls from a greater height, it has more energy to transfer to spinning the propeller. More energy means the propeller spins longer.

prompt: A swimmer kicks off from the wall of a pool. As they push hard against the wall in one direction, they move forward through the water in the opposite direction. What caused the swimmer to move?
optionA: The forces pushing on the swimmer were balanced
optionB: The forces pushing on the swimmer were unbalanced
optionC: The force of gravity on the swimmer was equal to the force of the water
optionD: The force of friction was the only force acting on the swimmer
explanation: The swimmer moves because an unbalanced force is pushing them—the push against the wall is stronger than the resistance from the water. Unbalanced forces cause objects to move.

prompt: A bridge can be made from steel, wood, or stone. An engineer wants to know which material makes the strongest bridge. Which of the following is the best way for the engineer to determine which material is strongest?
optionA: The engineer builds one bridge from steel and tests it when a heavy truck crosses
optionB: The engineer asks construction workers which material they prefer to use
optionC: The engineer builds test bridges from each material and compares how much weight each one can hold before breaking
optionD: The engineer measures the temperature and humidity where bridges made from each material are located
explanation: To fairly compare materials, the engineer must test bridges made from each material using the same conditions and measurement method. This is a controlled comparison.

prompt: A student mixed sugar into a cup of tea and recorded the temperature, color, and smell before and after mixing. Which of the following questions was the student most likely investigating?
optionA: Can liquids have a taste?
optionB: Did the tea gain stored energy?
optionC: Did a chemical reaction take place?
optionD: How does temperature affect the color of tea?
explanation: A chemical reaction changes the properties of a substance, such as its color, temperature, and smell. By observing these changes, the student was testing whether a chemical reaction happened.

prompt: In a scooter, the axle is a metal rod that the wheels are attached to. What is the main function of the axle in a scooter?
optionA: It holds the deck and frame together
optionB: It spins and allows the wheels to turn
optionC: It keeps the scooter body off the ground
optionD: It adds weight to make the scooter more stable
explanation: The axle is a rod that wheels spin around. When you push the scooter forward, the axle rotates, which makes the wheels turn and moves you forward.

prompt: Long ago, sailors on ships used hand signals and horn sounds to communicate with other ships instead of using radio equipment. Which of the following is an advantage of using hand signals for communication instead of a radio?
optionA: The messages can be sent and received underwater
optionB: Sending the messages is faster than using a radio
optionC: The messages can be sent without needing to speak or share a language
optionD: The messages are secure and cannot be heard by anyone else
explanation: Hand signals can be understood by people who speak different languages because you don't need words. A radio requires speakers to understand the same language.

prompt: A wind turbine converts the moving air into electrical energy. Under which of the following conditions will a wind turbine produce the most electrical energy?
optionA: When the air temperature is 32-40°F
optionB: When the air temperature is 75-85°F
optionC: When the wind speed is 8-12 miles per hour
optionD: When the wind speed is 18-25 miles per hour
explanation: Faster winds carry more energy. Wind turbines produce the most electricity when the wind is blowing fastest, because moving air has more kinetic energy to convert.

prompt: A skateboarder rides down a hill, then up the other side. Their speed is 8 miles per hour part way up the hill, 5 miles per hour at the very top of the hill, and 12 miles per hour part way down the other side. A student says that the skateboard has the most kinetic energy when it is at the top of the hill. What evidence shows that this student's claim is incorrect?
optionA: The skateboard must be pushed to go up the hill
optionB: The skateboard has a constant weight at the top of the hill
optionC: The skateboard moves faster part way down the hill than at the top
optionD: The skateboard rolls without friction at the top of the hill
explanation: Kinetic energy depends on how fast an object is moving. The skateboard is moving faster (12 mph) part way down than at the top (5 mph), so it has more kinetic energy going down.

prompt: A metal rail runs along a subway platform. If lightning were to strike the rail, it must safely conduct electricity away from people and into the ground. What material should be used for this conductive rail?
optionA: Metal
optionB: Plastic
optionC: Rubber
optionD: Ceramic
explanation: Metal conducts electricity well and allows it to flow safely to the ground. Plastic, rubber, and ceramic are insulators—they block electricity and keep it from flowing.

prompt: Two rabbits with brown fur and long ears are bred together and have baby rabbits. One parent rabbit was trained to hop through a tunnel at a young age, and the other parent learned to come when called—things they were taught, not born knowing. Which of the following is a trait the baby rabbits would most likely inherit from their parents?
optionA: Brown fur color
optionB: The ability to hop through a tunnel
optionC: Coming when called
optionD: The skill to find food quickly
explanation: Fur color is inherited—it comes from the parents' genes. Trained behaviors like hopping through tunnels or coming when called must be learned; they are not passed down genetically.

prompt: Many factories and power plants release smoke and harmful gases into the air. Car engines also produce exhaust fumes. Ships and airplanes burn fuel that creates emissions. Which of these activities creates the most air pollution in a busy city?
optionA: Heavy traffic with many cars driving on busy roads
optionB: Rain falling and cleaning the air around buildings
optionC: Forests and trees growing in parks throughout the city
optionD: Wind blowing between skyscrapers and buildings
explanation: Cars and trucks release harmful exhaust gases when their engines burn fuel. In a busy city with heavy traffic, thousands of vehicles emit pollution continuously. While rain cleans air, forests help by absorbing pollution, and wind disperses it, the main source of air pollution in cities is vehicle emissions from cars, trucks, and buses.

prompt: A chicken lays eggs that hatch into chicks. Each chick has different feather colors—some are golden, some are brown, and some are speckled. What explains why the feathers of each chick look different from the others?
optionA: Each chick inherited different information from both parent chickens
optionB: Each chick inherited identical information from both parent chickens
optionC: Each chick inherited different information from only the mother chicken
optionD: Each chick inherited identical information from only the father chicken
explanation: Offspring inherit genetic information from both parents, and the combination of traits from each parent produces variation. This is why each chick has a different feather color pattern.

prompt: A gardener plants seeds from the same packet in two locations: one in a sunny garden with plenty of water, and one in a shady corner with little water. The plants in the sunny location grow much taller than the plants in the shade. Why do the plants have different heights?
optionA: only because of inherited traits from the seed
optionB: only because of environmental conditions like sunlight and water
optionC: because of both inherited traits and environmental conditions
optionD: neither inherited traits nor environmental conditions affect plant height
explanation: Plant height is determined by both the genes inherited from the parent plants and the environmental conditions where they grow, such as light and water availability.

prompt: A diagram shows the life cycle of a tomato plant: Stage 1 → Seedling → Stage 2 → Flowering plant → Stage 3 → (cycle continues). Which table correctly identifies what happens at stages 1, 2, and 3?
optionA: Stage 1 = flowering, Stage 2 = reproduction, Stage 3 = sprouting
optionB: Stage 1 = germination, Stage 2 = growth, Stage 3 = death or decomposition
optionC: Stage 1 = germination, Stage 2 = reproduction, Stage 3 = growth
optionD: Stage 1 = reproduction, Stage 2 = germination, Stage 3 = death
explanation: The life cycle of any organism follows the sequence: birth/germination, growth, reproduction, and death. For a tomato plant, the stages before the seedling is germination, during growth, and after flowering is seed production or death/decomposition.

prompt: Students sealed a container with 10 grams of sugar and 20 grams of water (container mass: 50 grams). They stirred the mixture until the sugar dissolved completely. When they weighed the sealed container again, the total mass was 80 grams—the same as before. What does this observation demonstrate?
optionA: Matter is conserved when substances are mixed in a closed system
optionB: Water evaporates when sugar is dissolved in it
optionC: Chemical reactions always produce heat
optionD: Sugar changes into a different substance when it dissolves
explanation: Even though the sugar dissolved and disappeared from sight, the total mass stayed the same because matter is conserved. In a closed system, the mass of all materials before and after mixing is equal.

prompt: A student has a mixture of iron nails, plastic beads, and sand all mixed together. The iron nails are gray and magnetic, the beads are colorful and not magnetic, and the sand is tan and not magnetic. Which method would best separate the iron nails from the other materials?
optionA: Sort by color using your eyes
optionB: Shake the mixture and let the sand settle first
optionC: Use a magnet to remove the nails
optionD: Submerge everything in water and remove floating objects
explanation: Iron nails are magnetic while plastic beads and sand are not. Using a magnet takes advantage of this different physical property to separate the nails from the rest of the mixture.

prompt: A world map shows the locations of thousands of earthquakes recorded over the past century. When examined closely, most earthquakes cluster in specific zones. Which statement best describes where these earthquakes occur?
optionA: in the middle of continents away from coastlines
optionB: randomly scattered throughout all ocean basins
optionC: along certain boundaries where Earth's crustal plates meet
optionD: along every single boundary where ocean and land meet
explanation: Earthquakes occur where tectonic plates collide, separate, or slide past each other. Not all plate boundaries have earthquakes, and not all earthquakes happen exactly at boundaries, but they cluster along certain plate boundary zones.

prompt: A town in an earthquake zone has many older buildings built before earthquake-safety codes existed. Engineers propose these solutions: (1) Add steel reinforcements to cracks in old walls and strengthen foundations, (2) Retrofit older buildings with flexible support systems to reduce damage during shaking, (3) Only build new structures on solid bedrock, (4) Build all new structures shorter and lighter. Most of the town's population still lives in the older buildings. Which two solutions would best protect the majority of residents RIGHT NOW?
optionA: Solutions 1 and 2
optionB: Solutions 2 and 3
optionC: Solutions 3 and 4
optionD: Solutions 1 and 4
explanation: Since most residents still live in older buildings that cannot be demolished, solutions that retrofit (repair and strengthen) those existing structures are most practical and protective for the immediate population.

prompt: A grass plant grows in a sunny field. The plant needs energy to survive and grow. Which statement correctly describes how the grass plant obtains and uses energy from its surroundings?
optionA: The plant absorbs energy from the sun and converts it into motion that helps it run away from animals
optionB: The plant absorbs water from the soil and this water is converted into energy shared with insects
optionC: The plant absorbs minerals from the soil and uses them as energy for all its cells
optionD: The plant captures sunlight and converts it into a usable form of energy for growth and survival
explanation: Plants use photosynthesis to capture light energy from the sun and convert it into chemical energy (glucose) that they can use to grow and maintain their cells.

prompt: Two insect species live in the same meadow and both feed on clover: Species X completes three generations (life cycles) within one year, while Species Y completes only one generation per year. Which statement is accurate?
optionA: Both species have identical life cycle stages and they all happen at the same time
optionB: Both species have the same stages but at different times throughout the year
optionC: Both species go through similar life cycle stages over one year, but they reproduce at different rates
optionD: Both species complete the same number of generations and take the same amount of time to develop
explanation: Both species have the same basic life cycle stages (egg, larva/nymph, adult), but Species X completes its cycle faster and produces more generations per year than Species Y. The number of generations differs even though the stages are similar.

prompt: A prairie ecosystem has become overgrown with dense shrubs and trees, covering wildflowers that prairie birds depend on for food and nesting. Conservationists use controlled burns to clear away dead brush and woody plants, mimicking natural fires that occurred long ago. How do controlled burns help a prairie bird species that depends on wildflowers to survive?
optionA: The burns remove competing shrubs and trees, allowing wildflower meadows to grow and provide food and habitat
optionB: The burns destroy all competing plants permanently so birds have unlimited nesting space
optionC: The burns force birds to migrate to safer locations with more resources
optionD: The burns create an environment too hot for birds to live in, but that is temporary
explanation: Controlled burns clear away woody plants and brush that would otherwise shade out and kill wildflowers. By restoring conditions where wildflowers thrive, the burns support the birds that depend on those flowers.

prompt: Earth is tilted on its axis as it orbits the Sun. On June 21 at a location far north on Earth, the sun is high in the sky and there are about 18 hours of daylight. On December 21 at that same location, the sun is low in the sky. Compared to June 21, how much daylight is there on December 21?
optionA: Much less daylight, because of Earth's tilt on its axis
optionB: Much less daylight, because Earth spins faster on its axis in winter
optionC: Much more daylight, because of Earth's tilt on its axis
optionD: Much more daylight, because Earth spins slower on its axis in winter
explanation: Earth's tilt causes seasonal changes in daylight. In June, the northern hemisphere is tilted toward the sun, giving long days. In December, it is tilted away, giving short days. The rotation rate does not change.

prompt: Two plastic rods are rubbed with wool cloth in the same way. When the rods are held close to each other, they push apart and move away from each other. What did rubbing with wool cloth do to the plastic rods?
optionA: Each rod became electrically charged, and the like charges pushed them apart
optionB: Each rod became magnetic, and magnets repelled each other
optionC: The wool transferred opposite charges to each rod, making them attract
optionD: The wool created heat that pushed the rods away from each other
explanation: Rubbing transfers electric charge to the plastic rods. When both rods have the same type of charge (both positive or both negative), they repel each other.

prompt: A student rubs a plastic comb with wool cloth, then holds it near some small pieces of paper resting on a table. The pieces of paper jump up toward the comb and do not fall back down immediately. Which statement best explains this observation?
optionA: The forces on the paper are balanced and cancel out to zero
optionB: The forces exerted on the comb and paper are equal and opposite
optionC: Friction between the paper and table is pulling the paper toward the comb
optionD: The electrostatic force from the comb pulling on the paper is stronger than gravity pulling the paper down
explanation: When the comb is charged, it exerts an electrostatic force on the light paper pieces. For the paper to move upward toward the comb, the electrostatic pulling force must be greater than the downward pull of gravity.

prompt: A student conducts an experiment where a magnet is held at different distances from iron filings to test how distance affects magnetic attraction. The student measures how many filings attach to the magnet at each distance and records the results. Why should the student repeat this same experiment several more times with another magnet of identical size and strength?
optionA: to test different materials like copper instead of iron
optionB: to verify that the first trial's results are reliable and not just a one-time accident
optionC: because repeating trials means using less data, which is more accurate
optionD: because scientific investigations are required to have exactly three trials, no more and no less
explanation: Repeating an experiment multiple times shows whether the results are consistent and reliable. If different trials give similar results, the findings are more trustworthy.

prompt: A student rubs a balloon with wool cloth until it becomes charged with static electricity. The student then holds the charged balloon 8 centimeters from a lightweight aluminum can resting on a smooth table. The can rolls toward the balloon across the table. Which observation provides evidence that energy was transferred or converted in this investigation?
optionA: The balloon was rubbed with a piece of wool cloth
optionB: The electric charge built up on the balloon during rubbing
optionC: The can moved across the table from the electrostatic force
optionD: The table was smooth and had no friction
explanation: The motion of the can demonstrates that the electrostatic energy stored in the charged balloon was transferred to the can as kinetic energy (motion). Energy transfer is evidenced by the can's movement.

prompt: Throughout the day, the position of a tree's shadow changes. In the morning, the shadow is long and points one way. By noon, the shadow is short. By late afternoon, the shadow is long again and points the opposite direction. Which best explains why the shadow's position and length change during the day?
optionA: Earth rotates on its axis
optionB: The atmosphere becomes thicker as the sun sets
optionC: The sun moves around Earth
optionD: The sun gets closer to Earth during the day
explanation: As Earth rotates on its axis, different parts of Earth face the sun at different times, causing the sun to appear to move across the sky. This makes shadows change position and length throughout the day.

prompt: A student shines a laser pointer through two clear plastic tubes. One tube is perfectly straight. The other tube is bent in the middle like an elbow. Through which tube, if any, will the laser light be visible on a screen beyond the tube?
optionA: Through the straight tube only, because light travels in a straight line
optionB: Through the bent tube only, because the curve helps focus the light
optionC: Through both tubes, because light can bounce around any shape
optionD: Through neither tube, because the plastic absorbs the light
explanation: Light travels in straight lines and cannot turn corners. The laser light will only pass through the straight tube and reach the screen; the bent tube will block the light path.

prompt: A student places different small objects in a bucket of water and watches to see which ones float: a pencil, an eraser, a plastic bead, a stone pebble, a piece of aluminum foil, and honey (in a sealed container). Which set of items will float because they are less dense than water?
optionA: Pencil, plastic bead, honey
optionB: Eraser, stone pebble, plastic bead
optionC: Stone pebble, eraser, honey
optionD: Pencil, aluminum foil, stone pebble
explanation: Objects float when they are less dense than water. Pencils (mostly wood), plastic beads, and honey-filled containers are all less dense than water, so they will float. Stone and erasers sink because they are denser than water.

prompt: A food chain is shown: clover plants → rabbits → foxes → eagles. What role do the clover plants have in this food chain?
optionA: They capture energy from the sun and provide food for consumers
optionB: They prevent eagles from eating too many foxes
optionC: They break down dead organisms into simpler substances
optionD: They eat the sun's energy and pass it to consumers
explanation: Clover plants are producers that capture the sun's energy through photosynthesis. They convert this energy into plant matter, which serves as food for consumers like rabbits further up the food chain.

prompt: A student sets up two identical wet cloths outdoors: one is placed in front of a strong fan, and the other is placed in direct sunlight. Both start wet but the student wants to find which dries faster. Which two forms of energy are being compared in this investigation?
optionA: Mechanical energy and thermal energy
optionB: Sound energy and thermal energy
optionC: Light energy and electrical energy
optionD: Electrical energy and sound energy
explanation: The fan provides mechanical energy (moving air) to carry away moisture, while the sun provides thermal energy (heat) to speed up water evaporation. By comparing these two, the student can see which form of energy more effectively dries the cloth.

prompt: A table shows information about five vegetables and the time they need to grow: Lettuce (5 days to sprout, 30-40 days to harvest), Tomato (8-10 days to sprout, 60-85 days to harvest), Carrot (10-14 days to sprout, 65-80 days to harvest), Spinach (5-7 days to sprout, 40-50 days to harvest), Pumpkin (7-10 days to sprout, 90-120 days to harvest). Which statement is supported by the data?
optionA: Lettuce is ready for harvest in less time than spinach
optionB: Pumpkins take the least time overall because their seeds are large
optionC: Carrots sprout fastest of all the vegetables
optionD: Spinach needs more total time to harvest than tomatoes
explanation: According to the table, lettuce takes 30-40 days to harvest, while spinach takes 40-50 days. Lettuce is therefore ready for harvest sooner than spinach.

prompt: A student builds a model of the solar system in the gymnasium, with the clock on the wall representing the sun. The student must place model planets at their correct distances from the sun. Which planet should be placed at the greatest distance from the clock?
optionA: Venus
optionB: Saturn
optionC: Jupiter
optionD: Neptune
explanation: Neptune is the farthest planet from the sun in our solar system. In a scale model of the solar system, Neptune would need to be placed at the greatest distance from the sun representation.

prompt: A student observes a young hamster in a cage and records: it grooms its fur by licking its paws, it runs on its exercise wheel, it pushes food pellets into its cheek pouches, it eats from a food dish that the student sets out daily. Which observation is most likely a LEARNED behavior rather than an instinctive one?
optionA: Grooming its fur by licking its paws
optionB: Running on the exercise wheel
optionC: Pushing food into its cheek pouches
optionD: Eating from a specific food dish provided by the student
explanation: Hamsters have instinctive behaviors like grooming, running, and storing food in their cheeks. However, eating from a specific dish is a learned behavior because the hamster must learn to find and use the particular food dish the student provides.

prompt: A student reads the definition: 'the process by which water vapor in the air cools and turns into liquid water droplets.' Which term describes this process in the water cycle?
optionA: Evaporation
optionB: Precipitation
optionC: Sublimation
optionD: Condensation
explanation: Condensation is the process where water vapor in the atmosphere cools and transforms into liquid water droplets, forming clouds and dew.

prompt: A marine biologist studies dolphins in the ocean and gathers these observations: dolphins can echo-locate using sound waves, dolphins swim in warm ocean currents, dolphins hunt and eat fish, dolphins rest on sandy ocean bottoms. Which observation describes dolphins interacting with a LIVING element of their ecosystem?
optionA: Dolphins swim in warm ocean currents
optionB: Dolphins can echo-locate using sound waves
optionC: Dolphins rest on sandy ocean bottoms
optionD: Dolphins hunt and eat fish
explanation: Biotic interactions involve living things. Hunting and eating fish is a living interaction because both dolphins and fish are living organisms. Currents and sandy bottoms are abiotic (non-living) parts of the environment.

prompt: Four examples of objects or activities using different types of energy: Example 1) spinning bicycle wheels, Example 2) burning wood in a fireplace, Example 3) pushing a moving swing higher, Example 4) a robot arm lifting a box. Which examples use MECHANICAL energy to perform their function?
optionA: Examples 1, 2, and 4
optionB: Examples 1, 3, and 4
optionC: Examples 2 and 3 only
optionD: Examples 1 and 2 only
explanation: Mechanical energy is energy of motion. Spinning wheels (1), pushing a swing (3), and a robot arm lifting (4) all use motion-based mechanical energy. Burning wood (2) is chemical energy released as thermal energy.

prompt: A hummingbird has a long, thin, pointed beak for sipping nectar from flowers. A woodpecker has a strong, thick beak for pecking through bark to find insects. The difference between the shapes of their beaks is most likely related to the:
optionA: Different parts of the forest where they live
optionB: Different sizes of the birds
optionC: Different predators that hunt them
optionD: Different ways they find and eat their food
explanation: The beak structure of each bird is adapted to how it obtains food. Hummingbirds need long beaks to drink nectar, while woodpeckers need strong beaks to drill for insects. This structural difference directly relates to their feeding methods.

prompt: A student is classifying materials. Answering which question will provide the BEST evidence that an unknown object is a metal?
optionA: Does the object have a shiny appearance?
optionB: How much does the object weigh?
optionC: Does the object conduct (transfer) thermal energy quickly?
optionD: How quickly does the object dissolve in water?
explanation: Metals are excellent conductors of thermal energy. This property is fundamental to metals and distinguishes them from most other materials. While shininess and weight vary, thermal conductivity is a reliable identifying property of metals.

prompt: A biologist observes a squirrel in a park and records these observations: 1) climbing the tree trunk, 2) eating acorns from an oak tree, 3) burying acorns in the soil, 4) running across the ground, 5) drinking water from a puddle, 6) startled by a passing hawk. Which TWO observations best describe how the squirrel interacts with LIVING parts of its environment?
optionA: Observations 4 and 5
optionB: Observations 2 and 6
optionC: Observations 1 and 3
optionD: Observations 3 and 5
explanation: Biotic interactions involve living organisms. Eating acorns (2) is an interaction with a living tree, and being startled by a hawk (6) is an interaction with another living animal. The other observations involve non-living elements like soil, water, and the ground.

prompt: A student pours 8 grams of salt into a jar containing 250 milliliters of water and stirs for one minute. Which change most likely occurs to the salt when added to the water?
optionA: The salt breaks down to form new substances
optionB: The salt turns the water into a different liquid
optionC: The salt completely dissolves to form a saltwater solution
optionD: The salt floats on the surface of the water
explanation: When salt dissolves in water, it mixes uniformly throughout the water to form a solution. This is a physical change, not a chemical change, because no new substances are created—only the distribution of salt particles in water.

prompt: A student looks at a small insect through a magnifying glass lens. Which statement describes what happens to the light rays as they pass through the magnifying glass?
optionA: Light travels through the lens without changing direction
optionB: Light travels in straight lines and cannot be affected by the lens
optionC: Light bends (refracts) as it passes through the curved lens
optionD: Light bounces off the lens and cannot pass through
explanation: When light passes through a curved lens like a magnifying glass, it bends (refracts). This bending of light rays is what allows the lens to magnify objects, making them appear larger.

prompt: A student lists different energy sources used to generate electricity: Solar power, Natural gas, Geothermal energy, Oil, Tidal power. Which of these sources are RENEWABLE resources?
optionA: Solar power, geothermal energy, and tidal power
optionB: Natural gas, oil, and solar power
optionC: Solar power and oil only
optionD: Natural gas, geothermal energy, and tidal power
explanation: Renewable resources naturally replenish and do not run out. Solar power (from the sun), geothermal energy (from Earth's heat), and tidal power (from ocean tides) are all renewable. Natural gas and oil are non-renewable fossil fuels.

prompt: Bees have long, brush-like structures on their legs for collecting pollen. Beetles also have similar brush-like structures on their legs. Which statement best describes why bees and beetles both have these structures?
optionA: Both insects are the same size and shape
optionB: Both insects have the same predators
optionC: Both insects use the structures to collect the same food source: pollen
optionD: Both insects migrate to the same locations each year
explanation: Bees and beetles both interact with flowers and pollen as a food source. Their similar brush-like structures (called pollen baskets in bees, scopae in beetles) are adaptations for collecting and carrying pollen from flowers.

prompt: A student grinds a sample of an unknown mineral into a fine powder, mixes it with water, and then holds a magnet near the mixture. The student observes that some of the powder sticks to the magnet. Which conclusion is most supported by this observation?
optionA: The mineral contains copper
optionB: The mineral contains iron
optionC: The mineral contains aluminum
optionD: The mineral contains salt
explanation: Iron and its compounds are magnetic and are attracted to magnets. When the powder sticks to the magnet, it indicates the presence of iron in the mineral. This is a simple and effective way to test for iron.

prompt: The taiga biome has extremely cold winters with temperatures dropping to -40°C or lower, moderate snowfall, short summers, and evergreen forests. Based on these characteristics, which pair of animals is LEAST likely to live in the taiga?
optionA: Moose and lynx
optionB: Elk and black bear
optionC: Flamingo and crocodile
optionD: Porcupine and wolf
explanation: Flamingos are tropical wading birds and crocodiles are warm-water reptiles; both require warm climates and would not survive the extreme cold of the taiga. Moose, lynx, elk, bears, porcupines, and wolves are all adapted to cold forests.

prompt: A student creates a model showing Earth (a globe), the sun (a lamp), and the moon (a ball) to demonstrate the cycle of day and night. Which action should the student perform with the model objects to show one complete day-night cycle on Earth?
optionA: Move the lamp around the globe once
optionB: Move the moon around the globe once
optionC: Spin the globe on its axis once
optionD: Move the globe around the lamp once
explanation: One complete day-night cycle is caused by Earth rotating on its axis one full time. Spinning the globe once on its axis will demonstrate this rotation and show how different parts of Earth experience day and night.

prompt: Paleontologists discover fossils of coral reefs in rock layers deep underground in the middle of a desert. Modern-day coral reefs only grow in warm, shallow ocean water. What does this fossil discovery suggest about the history of this desert region?
optionA: The area has always been a dry desert
optionB: The area was once covered by a warm, shallow ocean or sea
optionC: Humans brought coral to this location thousands of years ago
optionD: The area was once extremely cold and covered with glaciers
explanation: Fossil corals only form in warm ocean environments. The presence of coral fossils in a desert indicates that this area was once underwater with warm ocean conditions, which has since changed dramatically.

prompt: Which land formation is correctly paired with the geological force that created it?
optionA: A deep canyon was formed by wind erosion over time
optionB: A volcanic mountain was formed by a river cutting through rock
optionC: A river delta was formed by glaciers moving across land
optionD: A deep valley was carved by a river flowing and cutting through rock layers
explanation: Rivers flowing over millions of years carve deep valleys and canyons through rock layers by erosion. This is the correct pairing of a land formation with the geological force that creates it.

prompt: A student captures several insects in a garden and studies them: a ladybug has its shell cracked, a butterfly has the typical yellow-and-black striped pattern of its species, a grasshopper has all six legs intact, a beetle has green coloring. Which characteristic is most likely an ACQUIRED trait (not inherited)?
optionA: The ladybug's cracked shell
optionB: The butterfly's yellow-and-black stripes
optionC: The grasshopper's six legs
optionD: The beetle's green coloring
explanation: A cracked shell is an injury or damage that the ladybug acquired during its life, not a trait passed down genetically. The stripe pattern, number of legs, and body color are inherited traits determined by genetics.

prompt: A gardener tests how quickly water drains through different soil types. Starting with 200 mL of water poured on each soil sample: Sandy soil drains 180 mL through and retains 20 mL, Clay soil drains 60 mL through and retains 140 mL, Loamy soil drains 150 mL through and retains 50 mL, Gravel drains 195 mL through and retains 5 mL. The gardener wants to plant a vegetable garden that needs soil that does NOT hold too much water. Which two soil types would be best for this garden?
optionA: Sandy soil and clay soil
optionB: Sandy soil and gravel
optionC: Gravel and loamy soil
optionD: Loamy soil and clay soil
explanation: Sandy soil and gravel both drain water very quickly (retaining only 20 mL and 5 mL respectively), which prevents excess water buildup. These are ideal for plants that prefer drier conditions. Clay holds too much water.

prompt: A student pours equal volumes of water and honey into a clear jar, stirs the mixture for ten seconds, and then lets it rest for five minutes. After resting, the honey settles to the bottom and the water sits on top, forming two distinct layers. Which conclusion best describes this observation?
optionA: Honey is less dense than water
optionB: Water is less dense than honey
optionC: Honey and water are equally dense
optionD: Density cannot be determined from this experiment
explanation: When two liquids are mixed, the less dense liquid floats on top and the denser liquid sinks to the bottom. Since water floats above the honey, water is less dense than honey.

prompt: Large coal deposits are found underground in certain regions of the world. How did these coal deposits most likely form?
optionA: Heat from deep within Earth transformed rocks into coal
optionB: Dead plants from ancient forests were buried, compressed, and heated over millions of years
optionC: Animals that died millions of years ago were crushed and turned into coal
optionD: Coal formed when volcanoes erupted and deposited dark ash
explanation: Coal forms from the remains of plants (especially trees) that lived in ancient swamps. Over millions of years, these plants were buried under layers of sediment, compressed, and heated, transforming into coal.

prompt: A student builds a simple rocket by taping an inflated balloon to a plastic straw attached to a car-shaped object. When the balloon is released, air rushes backward out of the straw, pushing the car forward. Which statement correctly describes the motion of the car based on this action-reaction pair?
optionA: The car moves in the same direction as the escaping air
optionB: The car moves in the opposite direction from the escaping air
optionC: The car only moves because the balloon becomes lighter as air escapes
optionD: The car does not move because forces inside the balloon cancel out
explanation: According to Newton's third law, for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. When air is expelled backward from the balloon, the car experiences a reaction force pushing it forward, in the opposite direction.

prompt: A student is given three objects: a brass key, an aluminum foil square, and a steel bolt. The student is asked to identify properties that ALL THREE objects share because they are metals. Which properties do all three metal objects have in common?
optionA: They bend easily, they are attracted to magnets, they conduct electricity
optionB: They dissolve in water, they are shiny, they float
optionC: They conduct electrical energy, they conduct thermal energy, they do not dissolve in water
optionD: They are attracted to magnets, they are heavy, they break easily
explanation: All metals conduct both electrical and thermal energy well. All three objects (brass, aluminum, steel) share these properties. Not all metals are magnetic (brass and aluminum are not magnetic), and not all are equally bendable or heavy.

prompt: A fast-growing, non-native water plant now grows in many lakes and can quickly spread across the entire water surface. Which effect will most likely occur when this invasive plant completely covers the surface of a lake?
optionA: Fish will have more places to hide and will increase in number
optionB: Less sunlight will be able to reach the aquatic plants growing underwater
optionC: All the native water plants will migrate to other lakes
optionD: Aquatic animals will gain a new food source and grow larger
explanation: When the invasive plant covers the lake surface, it blocks sunlight from reaching native aquatic plants below. This reduces their ability to photosynthesize and disrupts the ecosystem's food chain.

prompt: Students want to investigate how surface texture affects the speed at which objects slide. Which experimental design will BEST test the effect of surface texture while controlling all other variables?
optionA: Release two different-sized balls from the same height on the same smooth surface
optionB: Roll a ball down three different ramps with different angles from the same starting point with the same force
optionC: Roll the same ball down a smooth surface, a rough surface, and a carpeted surface from the same starting point and same height with the same force
optionD: Drop a ball from different heights onto the same surface and measure how far it bounces
explanation: A good controlled experiment changes only ONE variable (surface texture in this case) while keeping all other variables constant (same ball, same starting point, same height, same force). Option C correctly tests only surface texture while controlling other factors.

prompt: A nature documentary showed a herd of zebras at a watering hole. Two paths lead away from the water—one toward a savanna region where lions once chased and injured the herd, and another toward a grassland where lions have never been spotted. The zebras avoid the first path and choose the second. Which type of information processing allows the herd to make this choice?
optionA: Using memories stored in the brain to recall where lions have attacked before
optionB: Using memories stored in the legs to recall where lions attacked in the past
optionC: Using memories stored in the hooves to choose paths with the most grass
optionD: Using memories stored in the heart to avoid grasslands with many trees
explanation: The zebras' brains store memories of past encounters with lions, allowing them to recognize and avoid dangerous territory. Memory storage in the brain—not in body parts—enables this decision.

prompt: A student dropped a rock from different heights above a pond and measured its speed just before hitting the water. Data showed: dropped from 0.75 m, speed 3.84 m/s; dropped from 1.25 m, speed 4.95 m/s; dropped from 1.75 m, speed 5.86 m/s. Which statement about forces acting on the rock is supported by this data?
optionA: Balanced forces cause the rock's speed to increase as the release height increases
optionB: Unbalanced forces cause the rock's speed to increase as the rock falls
optionC: Forces on the rock are balanced when the rock is falling downward
optionD: Unbalanced forces cause the rock's speed to decrease as it falls toward the water
explanation: The data shows that speed increases with drop height, demonstrating that unbalanced gravitational force accelerates the rock throughout the fall, causing continuous speed increase.

prompt: A student claims that energy was converted from one form to another when a hammer struck an anvil. Which statement accurately describes an energy conversion that occurred and the supporting evidence?
optionA: Motion energy converted into sound energy; evidence: the hammer and anvil made a loud noise
optionB: Potential energy converted into light energy; evidence: sparks flew from the anvil
optionC: Heat energy converted into light energy; evidence: the anvil became very bright and shiny
optionD: Sound energy converted into motion energy; evidence: the anvil moved when struck
explanation: The hammer's motion energy converts to sound energy when it strikes the anvil, which is directly evidenced by the loud noise produced at impact.

prompt: A marble rolls down a ramp and collides with an identical marble at rest on a table. Which statement correctly predicts the changes in energy and motion when the two marbles collide?
optionA: The rolling marble transfers no energy to the stationary marble; the rolling marble stops while the stationary marble moves at the rolling marble's original speed
optionB: The rolling marble transfers no energy to the stationary marble; both marbles stop moving
optionC: The rolling marble transfers some of its energy to the stationary marble; the rolling marble keeps moving at its original speed while the stationary marble also moves
optionD: The rolling marble transfers some of its energy to the stationary marble; the rolling marble slows down while the stationary marble gains speed
explanation: During collision, the rolling marble transfers part of its energy and momentum to the stationary marble. The first marble loses speed and the second marble gains speed.

prompt: A coastal town experienced severe erosion when a large storm surge occurred, damaging homes and roads near the shoreline. Which design solution would require the FEWEST steps to reduce future impacts of storm surge on residents?
optionA: Build a series of new neighborhoods inland and relocate all residents to higher elevation areas
optionB: Distribute sandbags to residents to place as temporary barriers against future storm surges
optionC: Maintain existing seawalls and drainage systems that already channel water safely away from populated areas
optionD: Plant hundreds of trees and grasses along the shoreline to slow wave energy
explanation: Using existing infrastructure (seawalls and drainage systems) requires the fewest implementation steps—maintaining what already exists is simpler than building new systems or physically moving populations.

prompt: After a period of heavy rainfall, a photograph showed a portion of a bridge where one support pillar had tilted and cracked. How did the heavy rainfall most likely cause this damage to the bridge structure?
optionA: Heavy rain made the pillar expand and split from water absorption
optionB: Underground water flow eroded soil beneath the pillar's foundation, causing it to shift and crack
optionC: Lightning during the storm weakened the concrete support pillar
optionD: Floodwater rushing over the bridge crushed the pillar into pieces
explanation: Water moving through soil underneath the bridge foundation erodes the support material, causing the foundation to weaken and the pillar to settle unevenly, resulting in cracks.

prompt: Students placed a piece of limestone in a dish, added drops of vinegar, and observed what happened. Before adding vinegar, the total mass (limestone, vinegar, dish) was 22.40 grams; after the reaction with fizzing, the total mass was 21.15 grams. A student claims a new substance was formed. Which observation is evidence supporting this claim?
optionA: Fizzing and bubbles formed after the vinegar was added to the limestone
optionB: The limestone became smaller in size but remained the same shape
optionC: The limestone changed from white to gray after the vinegar was added
optionD: The vinegar caused the limestone to melt and lose mass as liquid
explanation: Bubbling and fizzing indicate that a gas is being produced, which is evidence that a chemical reaction has created a new substance (carbon dioxide gas in this case).

prompt: A student recorded facts about a prairie dog's senses: Fact 1: Sharp hearing allows the prairie dog to detect alarm calls from nearby prairie dogs warning of danger. Fact 2: The prairie dog can close its nostrils when burrowing to keep out dust and dirt. Fact 3: Excellent vision helps the prairie dog spot hawks flying overhead. Fact 4: A keen sense of smell helps the prairie dog find seeds underground for food. Which facts provide evidence that the prairie dog uses sense organs to detect threats from OTHER organisms?
optionA: facts 1 and 3
optionB: facts 2 and 4
optionC: facts 1 and 2
optionD: facts 3 and 4
explanation: Facts 1 and 3 both describe detecting threats: hearing alarm calls from other prairie dogs and seeing predatory hawks. Facts 2 and 4 relate to self-protection and finding food, not detecting threats.

prompt: Which row correctly pairs a claim about arctic animals with a logical solution to help them survive in warming conditions? Row 1: Claim - less ice coverage will reduce hunting areas; Solution - build enclosed habitats to replace melting ice. Row 2: Claim - warming temperatures threaten animal survival; Solution - introduce animals from tropical regions to compete with arctic species. Row 3: Claim - arctic animals face food shortages in warming conditions; Solution - identify population areas and establish protected food sources like vegetation and prey reserves. Row 4: Claim - as ice melts, populations will adapt quickly; Solution - provide artificial ice rinks in the arctic to replace lost sea ice.
optionA: Row 1
optionB: Row 2
optionC: Row 3
optionD: Row 4
explanation: Row 3 pairs a realistic problem (food shortages) with a logical, practical solution (establishing food reserves). The other rows either misdiagnose the problem or propose solutions that are unrealistic or could make conditions worse.

prompt: A student made a device with an electromagnet and measured how many metal beads the electromagnet could hold when connected to a battery. The student then placed the electromagnet at different distances (1 cm, 2 cm, 3 cm, 4 cm away from a pile of beads) and recorded how many beads were pulled toward the electromagnet at each distance. Which question is the student investigating?
optionA: How does the color of the electromagnet wire affect the strength of the magnetic field?
optionB: How is the strength of the magnetic force on nearby objects affected by the distance between the electromagnet and the objects?
optionC: How does the temperature of the battery affect the magnetic force exerted by an electromagnet?
optionD: What types of materials can be attracted to an electromagnet compared to a permanent magnet?
explanation: The student is systematically changing distance while measuring the number of beads attracted, directly investigating the relationship between distance and magnetic force strength.

prompt: In an investigation using one electromagnet, the results showed: at 0 cm distance: 23 metal beads held, at 1 cm: 15 beads, at 2 cm: 8 beads, at 3 cm: 4 beads, at 4 cm: 2 beads (magnetic force decreases as distance increases). The student repeats the investigation using a stronger electromagnet (double coils on the same battery). Which table shows the most likely results for the stronger electromagnet trial, given that a stronger electromagnet should hold more beads at every distance than the single electromagnet did?
optionA: 0 cm: 23, 1 cm: 15, 2 cm: 8, 3 cm: 4, 4 cm: 2 (identical to the single-electromagnet results)
optionB: 0 cm: 20, 1 cm: 12, 2 cm: 6, 3 cm: 3, 4 cm: 1 (lower at every distance)
optionC: 0 cm: 28, 1 cm: 19, 2 cm: 11, 3 cm: 6, 4 cm: 3 (higher at every distance, still decreasing overall)
optionD: 0 cm: 28, 1 cm: 8, 2 cm: 15, 3 cm: 5, 4 cm: 2 (values do not show a consistent pattern)
explanation: A stronger electromagnet should attract more beads at every distance compared to the weaker one. The pattern must still show decreasing values as distance increases, maintaining the trend from the original investigation.

prompt: A student built an electromagnet by wrapping wire around a steel rod and connecting it to a battery, then tested how many nails it could lift using 3 coils of wire versus 5 coils of wire, and compared results using a 2-volt battery versus a 6-volt battery. The student wants to determine the relationship between battery voltage and the magnetic force exerted by the electromagnet. Which question was most likely being investigated?
optionA: How did changing the number of coils affect the number of nails lifted by the electromagnet when using only a 2-volt battery?
optionB: For the same number of coils, how did the number of nails lifted when using a 2-volt battery compare to the number lifted when using a 6-volt battery?
optionC: How does keeping the voltage constant at 6 volts affect the number of nails lifted as the number of coils increases?
optionD: For different numbers of coils, how did the number of nails lifted change with the 2-volt battery compared to changes with the 6-volt battery?
explanation: To test the relationship between voltage and magnetic force, the student must hold the number of coils constant and vary only the voltage. Option B describes this specific controlled comparison.

prompt: A student wants to get accurate data about how many rubber bands an electromagnet can stretch. How would performing more trials in this investigation improve the reliability of the data collected?
optionA: More trials produce more measurements, which can help reduce errors caused by measurement mistakes or variations in the setup
optionB: More trials always produce identical data, eliminating the need to repeat measurements
optionC: Averaging data from more trials can help determine which equipment to use
optionD: Averaging data from more than three trials always reduces the accuracy of the result
explanation: Repeated trials allow researchers to identify and average out random errors that might occur in individual measurements, making the final result more trustworthy.

prompt: Your body breaks down the apple you eat for breakfast into tiny pieces inside your cells. These pieces then get combined with a gas you breathe in through your lungs. This process releases heat that keeps you warm, plus other materials that leave your body through your breath and sweat. What are the THREE main things needed for this cell-power process to work?
optionA: The food from the apple, the oxygen from the air, and the cell releases energy
optionB: The food from the apple, carbon dioxide, and stored heat from the sun
optionC: Oxygen from the air, water from the apple, and energy the cell creates by itself
optionD: Energy from heat, oxygen from the air, and carbon dioxide from the soil
explanation: When your body breaks down food (like an apple), it combines the food with oxygen you breathe in. This makes energy your cells can use, plus carbon dioxide (which you breathe out) and water (which you sweat out).

prompt: A school needs to clear ice from a walkway next to a playground where kids play in winter. The school tested four different materials to see which works best: salt, rock salt crystals, urea, and sand. They measured three things: how much money each costs, how quickly each melted the ice, and whether it hurt the nearby plants. The rock salt crystals worked fastest and could melt ice even when it was extremely cold outside. However, one of the other materials was cheaper. Based on the school's testing, why did they choose to use rock salt crystals instead of the cheaper choice?
optionA: Because it did not harm any plants at all
optionB: Because it melted ice faster and worked in the coldest weather, even though it cost more money
optionC: Because sand could not melt ice no matter how cold it was
optionD: Because urea was too expensive for the school budget
explanation: The school picked rock salt crystals because it did the best job melting ice in extreme cold—that matters more for safety than saving money. Even though another material cost less, rock salt crystals' superior performance was worth the extra cost.

prompt: A gardener is growing vegetables next to the school playground. Every winter, the path gets icy and slippery. The gardener tested materials to spread on the ice: regular salt works okay but kills plants, rock salt works great but also damages plants, a special powder called urea takes 20 minutes to melt ice at cold temperatures but does NOT hurt plants, and sand does nothing to melt ice but is completely safe for plants. The path must: (1) actually melt the ice, and (2) keep the garden plants alive. Which single material should the gardener pick?
optionA: Sand, because it will not hurt the plants
optionB: Regular salt, because it is easy to find
optionC: Urea, because it melts ice and does not damage the garden
optionD: Rock salt, because it works fastest at any temperature
explanation: Urea is the only material that does both jobs: it actually melts ice (unlike sand) and it doesn't harm the plants (unlike regular salt and rock salt). Even though it takes 20 minutes, it's the right choice for a garden.

prompt: A scientist is studying the location of genes inside human body cells. Genes carry instructions for traits like hair color and eye shape. Inside which part of the cell would you find the structure that holds all of a person's genes?
optionA: The cell membrane that covers the outside of the cell
optionB: The thick liquid inside the cell
optionC: The part of the cell that stores water
optionD: The control center of the cell where instructions are stored
explanation: Genes are stored inside the cell's control center (called the nucleus). The nucleus is like the brain of the cell—it holds all the instructions for what the cell should do and what traits your body will have.

prompt: Two children have the same mother and father. One child has dark brown eyes and the other has light blue eyes. The parents notice their eyes are different colors even though they come from the same family. Which best explains why each child has a different eye color?
optionA: Each child inherited different instructions from their parents that cause their body to make different colored proteins in their eyes
optionB: Each child received a completely different number of genes from their parents
optionC: One child's eyes changed color as they grew older
optionD: Each child got a different number of chromosomes from one parent
explanation: Eye color depends on which versions of genes you inherit. Different gene versions make different proteins, which creates different eye colors. Both kids have the same number of genes and chromosomes—they just inherited different versions of the eye-color genes.

prompt: Heat can move from one place to another in different ways. Which of these examples shows heat moving mainly through DIRECT TOUCHING between two materials?
optionA: When the sun's light bounces off a mirror
optionB: When hot melted rock from inside the Earth touches cold rock surrounding it
optionC: When warm air rises up and carries heat across a room
optionD: When warm water currents in the ocean move north
explanation: Heat moves through direct contact when two materials touch each other—like when hot melted rock touches cold rock. This is called conduction. Light bouncing is radiation, and moving air or water carrying heat is convection, not direct touching.

prompt: A scientist performs four different chemical reactions in sealed containers and measures the total weight before and after each reaction. In Container A, the weight dropped from 100g to 97g. In Container B, the weight dropped from 140g to 138g. In Container C, the weight went up from 120g to 121g. In Container D, the weight stayed exactly the same at 150g before and after. Which container was most likely completely sealed with nothing able to escape or enter?
optionA: Container A, because the weight decreased
optionB: Container B, because the weight change was small
optionC: Container C, because the weight increased
optionD: Container D, because the total amount of material did not change
explanation: In a completely sealed system, matter cannot escape or enter, so the total weight stays exactly the same. Container D is the sealed system because its weight didn't change—all the material stayed inside the container.

prompt: Plant cells contain many tiny structures, each with its own job. One type of structure is found in BOTH plant cells and animal cells. Its main job is to take the food that the cell has and break it down into usable energy. What is this structure's primary role?
optionA: To store water in the plant cells
optionB: To make new cells by splitting into two
optionC: To provide the cell with energy it needs to work
optionD: To remove harmful waste products from the cell
explanation: This structure is called the mitochondrion (or mitochondria in plural). It is like a tiny power plant inside your cells. It takes nutrients and breaks them down to release energy that the cell uses to do its jobs.

prompt: Scientists noticed that a common bacteria species was becoming less able to be killed by a certain medicine over many years. In 1999, about 95% of the bacteria could be killed by the medicine. By 2015, only about 65% could be killed. The bacteria had not decided to change themselves. Instead, what happened to make the bacteria stronger against the medicine?
optionA: The bacteria that could survive the medicine made more copies of themselves and passed this survival ability to their offspring, while the weaker bacteria died off
optionB: The bacteria became stronger because they tried harder to survive each time they were exposed to the medicine
optionC: The medicine got weaker over time and could no longer kill bacteria effectively
optionD: All of the bacteria changed their bodies in the same way to protect themselves from the medicine
explanation: This is natural selection. Some bacteria naturally had genes that protected them from the medicine. These bacteria survived and had more babies, passing on protection genes. Over generations, more and more bacteria inherited this protection, so fewer could be killed by the medicine. The bacteria didn't choose to change—the stronger ones just had more babies.

prompt: Deep under the ocean floor, a diagram shows two giant pieces of the Earth's crust moving apart from each other. Hot, flowing material from deep inside the Earth is shown rising up between them, pushing the crust pieces away from each other on both sides. What force is pushing these enormous pieces of crust in opposite directions?
optionA: Waves of cold material sinking from the top of the ocean
optionB: Circular movement of hot material inside the Earth rising, spreading sideways, and sinking back down
optionC: Explosive pressure from rocks melting at the Earth's center
optionD: The spinning rotation of the Earth itself
explanation: The crust moves because of convection currents in the mantle—the layer below the crust. Hot material rises up at the ridge, spreads sideways and pushes the crust apart, then cools and sinks back down. This circle of moving material is what forces the plates to separate.

prompt: A weather scientist compares two cities: San Diego is right next to the Pacific Ocean on the California coast, while Phoenix is far inland in the desert. The scientist notices that San Diego's summers are much cooler than Phoenix's summers, even though they are at almost the same distance from the equator. What is the main reason San Diego stays cooler in summer?
optionA: Because San Diego is at a higher elevation than Phoenix
optionB: Because the nearby ocean water absorbs and stores heat, keeping the air cooler than it would be far from water
optionC: Because San Diego gets much more rain than Phoenix
optionD: Because the Pacific Ocean creates fog that blocks the sun
explanation: Large bodies of water like oceans heat up and cool down much more slowly than land. In summer, the ocean stays cool, and winds blow cool ocean air toward San Diego, keeping the city cooler. Inland cities like Phoenix have no water to cool them down, so summers get much hotter.

prompt: Scientists studied the fossils of ocean creatures found in rock layers spanning 600 million years. They made a graph showing how many different groups of ocean animals lived at different times. The graph showed the number of animal groups gradually growing for most of history. Then, suddenly, at a point 250 million years ago, the number dropped sharply. After that drop, the numbers started rising again toward today. What does this sudden drop in the number of animal groups tell us happened at that time?
optionA: New ocean animals were first evolving and becoming common
optionB: A huge number of ocean animal groups suddenly disappeared, meaning far fewer species existed
optionC: Most ocean animals moved onto the land to escape something
optionD: Ocean animals adapted to major changes in their environment
explanation: When the number of animal groups in the fossil record drops suddenly like this, it means many species died out at the same time—a mass extinction. This shows that something terrible happened to ocean life 250 million years ago, killing most species. A sudden drop in diversity means extinction, not adaptation or evolution of new species.

prompt: A geologist is proving that the climate of a region has changed dramatically over millions of years. Which of these pieces of evidence would BEST show that the area was once much colder?
optionA: Large mountains in the area
optionB: Deep river valleys cutting through rock
optionC: Rocks and soil that were clearly scraped and left behind by moving glaciers
optionD: Dark volcanic rocks formed from cooled lava
explanation: Glacial deposits—rocks and soil left behind when glaciers melted—are the clearest proof that glaciers once covered the area. This shows it was much colder millions of years ago. Mountains can form for many reasons, rivers are always present, and volcanic rocks don't tell us about climate.

prompt: Scientists studied the bones of three very different animals—a tiger's front paw, a human's arm, and a frog's leg. Even though these animals look completely different on the outside and use their limbs in totally different ways, the bones are arranged in surprisingly the same pattern: one long bone, two bones next to each other, then a cluster of smaller bones at the end. What does this similarity in bone structure suggest about these three animals?
optionA: The frog's bones are the simplest and prove it evolved first before tigers and humans
optionB: All three animals have not changed their bones at all since they were first created
optionC: The three animals evolved from completely different sources but designed their bones the same way
optionD: These three animals share a common ancestor from long ago and inherited similar bone patterns from that shared relative
explanation: When different animals have the same basic bone structure even though they look and move differently, it's evidence they share an ancestor long ago. That shared ancestor passed down the same bone blueprint. Over time, this structure changed for each animal's specific needs, but the basic pattern stayed the same.

prompt: A dog breeder has two adult dogs with brown fur. When these dogs have puppies, some puppies have brown fur while others have black fur. Why don't all the puppies look like their parents?
optionA: Each puppy inherited a different mix of genes from both parents, creating unique combinations
optionB: Some puppies were born from a different father
optionC: Puppies with black fur came from asexual reproduction instead of sexual reproduction
optionD: All puppies develop the same way, but their fur changes color as they grow older
explanation: Sexual reproduction mixes genes from both parents in different ways for each offspring. This genetic mixing creates variation—even siblings can look different because each one gets a unique combination of traits.

prompt: Calcium and potassium are two elements that have very similar chemical behavior. What feature of their atoms explains why these elements react in similar ways?
optionA: They both have the same number of outer shell electrons
optionB: They both are found in the same state of matter at room temperature
optionC: They both have more neutrons than protons
optionD: They both have the same total number of electrons
explanation: The electrons on the outer edge of an atom determine how it reacts with other elements. When two elements have the same pattern of outer electrons, they behave similarly in chemical reactions.

prompt: A guide uses a special chart to identify beetles found in gardens. The chart asks: Does the beetle have wings? If yes, does it have one pair or two pairs of wings? For this beetle, the answer is: yes, two pairs of wings. Based on the chart, which group does this beetle belong to?
optionA: Flies and mosquitoes (one pair of wings)
optionB: Beetles (two pairs of wings)
optionC: Lice and fleas (no wings)
optionD: Butterflies (two wings that fold closed)
explanation: A dichotomous key is a step-by-step guide that narrows down what something is by asking yes/no questions. Each answer leads you to the next question until you reach the correct classification.

prompt: A scientist builds a tiny model of an atom using different colored balls. Red balls sit inside a sphere (the nucleus), while a blue ball moves in circles around the outside. What can you say about the electrical charges of these balls?
optionA: Both red balls are positive charges; the blue ball is negative
optionB: Both red balls are negative charges; the blue ball is positive
optionC: One red ball is positive and the other is neutral; the blue ball is negative
optionD: One red ball is positive and one is neutral; the blue ball is negative
explanation: Atoms have three main parts: protons (positive charge) and neutrons (no charge) in the nucleus, and electrons (negative charge) orbiting outside. The positive and negative charges balance each other out.

prompt: A child stands on a skateboard and pushes hard against a wall. As the wall pushes the child forward, what is the correct way to describe the forces involved?
optionA: The force of the child on the wall and the force of the wall on the child are action-reaction pairs
optionB: The child's push creates movement but the wall doesn't push back
optionC: Friction between the skateboard and ground is the only important force
optionD: The wall is stronger than the child so it moves in the opposite direction
explanation: Newton's third law says forces always come in pairs: when one object pushes on another, the second object pushes back just as hard. The child pushes the wall, and the wall pushes the child equally.

prompt: Farmers spray chemicals on crops to kill weeds and insects that damage the plants. These chemicals often wash into nearby rivers and streams. What is the best way for farmers to reduce harm to these waterways?
optionA: Use crops that require fewer chemical sprays
optionB: Plant more trees near the crops to use up extra water
optionC: Use more water to dilute the chemicals
optionD: Harvest crops earlier in the growing season
explanation: Fewer chemicals mean less pollution washing into waterways. Using crops and practices that need fewer chemicals protects the water quality in nearby streams and rivers.

prompt: A type of thick grass from Africa was introduced to grazing areas in the southwestern United States. This African grass grows faster and takes up more space than native grasses, making it hard for native plants to survive. What is most likely to happen to the native grasses in these areas over many years?
optionA: The population of native grasses will increase and outcompete the African grass
optionB: The population of native grasses will decrease because the African grass takes their space and water
optionC: The African grass will evolve to look like the native grasses to blend in
optionD: The native grasses will develop new traits to become more competitive
explanation: Invasive species compete with native species for the same resources—water, space, and sunlight. When an invasive species is more successful at surviving, native species gradually disappear from that area.

prompt: Two runners race along a straight track. Runner A runs 50 meters in 60 seconds. Runner B runs 25 meters in 60 seconds. If they keep running at the same speed, how far will each runner have gone after 120 seconds total?
optionA: Runner A: 90 meters, Runner B: 45 meters
optionB: Runner A: 75 meters, Runner B: 37.5 meters
optionC: Runner A: 120 meters, Runner B: 60 meters
optionD: Runner A: 100 meters, Runner B: 50 meters
explanation: To find distance at a new time, use the speed (distance ÷ time). Runner A is faster, so in double the time, each runner covers double the original distance.

prompt: A person picks up a 4-kilogram bowling ball and wants to accelerate it forward at a rate of 3 meters per second squared. What is the net force (in newtons) that must be applied to the bowling ball? (Use: Force = mass × acceleration)
optionA: 12 newtons
optionB: 7 newtons
optionC: 9 newtons
optionD: 15 newtons
explanation: Force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma). With mass = 4 kg and acceleration = 3 m/s², the force needed is 4 × 3 = 12 newtons. This is multi-step calculation thinking.

prompt: Scientists collected data on four elements' positions in the periodic table. Element A: Row 2, Column 1. Element B: Row 2, Column 2. Element C: Row 3, Column 1. Element D: Row 3, Column 2. Which element has the same number of electron energy levels as Element A?
optionA: Element B (also in Row 2)
optionB: Element C (in Row 3, same column as A)
optionC: Element D (in Row 3, same column as B)
optionD: All elements have the same number of energy levels
explanation: The row (horizontal line) in the periodic table tells you how many electron shells an atom has. Elements in the same row have the same number of energy levels.

prompt: A chemistry teacher writes out a balanced equation for a reaction: 2C₂H₆ + 7O₂ → 4CO₂ + 6H₂O. If you count all the oxygen atoms on both the left and right sides of this equation, how many oxygen atoms are there in total?
optionA: 7 oxygen atoms total
optionB: 11 oxygen atoms total
optionC: 14 oxygen atoms total
optionD: 20 oxygen atoms total
explanation: Count carefully: on the left side, 7O₂ molecules = 14 oxygen atoms. On the right side, 4CO₂ (8 atoms) + 6H₂O (6 atoms) = 14 atoms. Balanced equations have equal atoms on both sides.

prompt: Two plants grow side by side in the same garden. Plant A has a large root system that reaches deep underground with many branching roots. Plant B is a small plant with short, shallow roots. Why is Plant A better at finding water?
optionA: Plant A can absorb more water because its roots reach deeper and spread wider through the soil
optionB: Plant A gets more sunlight because its roots are deeper
optionC: Plant B absorbs more water because its shallow roots are closer to rainfall
optionD: Plant B gets more nutrients because its roots are closer to the surface
explanation: Larger, deeper root systems can reach water from a greater area of soil and from deeper underground where water is often available even during dry periods.

prompt: In a coastal habitat, energy flows through different organisms: tiny water plants and sea grasses (producers) → small shellfish (primary consumers) → fish (secondary consumers) → sharks (top consumers). Which statement correctly describes how energy moves through this food chain?
optionA: Fish get energy directly from both the water plants and the sharks
optionB: Sharks get energy directly from the tiny water plants
optionC: Sharks receive energy directly from the fish that eat the smaller animals
optionD: Water plants get energy from the shellfish and fish
explanation: In a food chain or food pyramid, energy flows upward one level at a time. Each consumer eats the level below it and is eaten by the level above. Energy doesn't skip levels.

prompt: A student uses a lamp, a ball, and a globe to demonstrate a solar eclipse. Which motion of the objects best shows what happens during a solar eclipse?
optionA: The ball moves between the lamp and globe, blocking the lamp's light from reaching the globe
optionB: The globe moves between the lamp and ball, casting a shadow on the ball
optionC: The lamp moves between the globe and ball, creating shadows on both
optionD: The ball orbits around the globe while the lamp stays still
explanation: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes directly between the Sun and Earth, blocking sunlight from reaching Earth. The Moon's shadow falls on Earth.

prompt: Plant and animal cells both have structures that surround them and keep water balanced inside the cell. What is the job that BOTH a plant cell wall AND an animal cell membrane perform?
optionA: Creating energy for the cell to use
optionB: Controlling the movement of water into and out of the cell
optionC: Storing genetic information to pass to offspring
optionD: Breaking down waste materials from the cell
explanation: Both cell membranes and cell walls act as barriers that separate the inside of the cell from the outside, and they both allow water and nutrients to move in and out in a controlled way.

prompt: A teacher mixes together a clear colorless liquid with a clear yellow liquid in a test tube. Suddenly, a thick orange solid forms and settles to the bottom. Which observation shows that a chemical reaction has taken place (not just a physical change)?
optionA: The mixture boils and steam rises from the test tube
optionB: The mixture stays in the test tube but becomes heavier
optionC: A completely new solid substance forms that wasn't there before
optionD: The liquids mix together and change color to orange
explanation: A chemical reaction creates new substances with different properties. When a solid forms from two liquids mixing, that's usually a sign of a chemical reaction that formed a new material.

prompt: If you look up at the night sky, the Sun appears much brighter than any other star, even though some stars are actually much bigger and hotter than the Sun. Why does the Sun seem so bright to us?
optionA: The Sun releases more energy than any other star
optionB: The Sun has unique chemical reactions that make brighter light
optionC: The Sun is much hotter than all other stars in the universe
optionD: The Sun is much closer to Earth than any other star
explanation: Brightness depends on distance as well as the star's actual brightness. The Sun appears brightest to us because it is by far the closest star to Earth—not because it is the biggest or hottest star overall.

prompt: Students exercise by jumping rope for one minute and measure their heart rate and breathing rate before and after. Their heart rate increases from 60 to 120 beats per minute, and their breathing rate increases from 15 to 35 breaths per minute. Which pair of body systems are working together to handle this exercise?
optionA: Nervous system adds oxygen to blood; Skeletal system removes carbon dioxide
optionB: Circulatory system pumps blood to carry oxygen and remove waste; Respiratory system brings oxygen into the blood and releases carbon dioxide
optionC: Digestive system provides energy; Skeletal system holds the body upright
optionD: Muscular system pumps blood; Nervous system controls all movement
explanation: During exercise, your heart pumps faster to deliver oxygen-rich blood to your muscles. Your breathing speeds up to bring more oxygen in through your lungs. The circulatory and respiratory systems work together.

prompt: A car engine burns fuel in a cylinder. The fuel releases heat energy that expands into hot gases. These hot gases push a piston down. The piston turns connected parts that make the wheels rotate. Which statement correctly describes the energy changes in this process?
optionA: Chemical energy from the fuel becomes heat energy, which then becomes movement energy
optionB: Heat energy from the fuel becomes mechanical energy, which becomes electrical energy
